chapter: Armstrong, Big Sid and Joe Glaser
title: Louis and the baby that was not his
summary: Louis saved coins in a bag for the child of a woman who claimed he was the father, and Lucille told him he could not have fathered a child, which Bigard offers to show how easily he was fooled.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: He wanted a kid so bad, and -- this is real funny. He had a little gal called Sweet -- Sweetie-something and she got pregnant but not by Louie. But Louie thought it was by him because she was telling him that, you know? And, oh, he was proud. He's going to be the daddy.

So he had a bag. We were traveling by bus now, and he had a bag and all the -- when he was getting ready to go to sleep -- all the change he had in his pocket plus dollars he'd take it, put it in his bag. I asked him what he was doing that for. He said, 'That's for my kid when it's born.' Okay, so by the time this kid was born that bag was stuffed with coins and dollars and fives and tens, just stuffed.

So he gave it to this little gal. Now the baby was born, oh, he was walking around like a peacock. So he started talking to Lucille again. He said, 'Lucille, how'd you feel if you adopt my kid?' She said, 'What kid?' He said, 'My kid. I got a baby by Sweetie.' She said, 'Who told you you got a baby by Sweetie? You better not bring no baby around here.'

She says, "You couldn't make a baby with a pencil. Now you're talking about your kid. She done fool you and she's got a boyfriend. He must have did it and he's telling her to tell you that you're the father." She said, "You sure are stupid." Well, that's how he was. He'd go for anything.

He put one gal in a beauty parlor. He bought Stuff Crouch a big -- this big car. Not a Dodge. What's the -- oh, Chrysler, the big Chrysler. [Imperial] He bought him that before he put him in business in that thing. Oh, he was something.
